The protocol as blocks to read

Source: R/protocol.R
collapse_protocol.Rd

comparison_protocol() is one row per interval, which a workout file needs and a rider does not. This collapses consecutive rows back into the blocks they came from, so the table on the Record tab and the one in vignette("recording_rides") are both the protocol rather than a transcription of it that can drift from the workout file.

Usage

collapse_protocol(protocol, ftp = 250)

Arguments

protocol

One row per interval, as comparison_protocol() returns.

ftp

Functional threshold power in watts, which turns the fractional targets into the watts the trainer will be asked to hold. The default is the package's reference rider; set your own.

Value

A data frame of Block, Duration, Mode, Target and Why, one row per block, with a closing Total.

Examples

collapse_protocol(comparison_protocol(), ftp = 250)
#>              Block         Duration           Mode
#> 1  Zero and settle             30 s              —
#> 2      Sync surges 4 × (8 s / 20 s) Level or slope
#> 3        Ladder up        5 × 2 min            Erg
#> 4            Coast            1 min              —
#> 5      Ladder down        5 × 2 min            Erg
#> 6    Stop together             30 s              —
#> 11           Total           24 min               
#>                                   Target
#> 1                               Coasting
#> 2          About 375 W, coasting between
#> 3  138 W → 175 W → 212 W → 250 W → 275 W
#> 4                               Coasting
#> 5  275 W → 250 W → 212 W → 175 W → 138 W
#> 6                               Coasting
#> 11                                      
#>                                                                                                         Why
#> 1                                                    A shared floor of true zeros at the head of every file
#> 2                                Coast-to-power edges, so check_alignment() can resolve rather than default
#> 3                                                               Several hundred stable seconds in each band
#> 4                                                                               Exercises the coasting drop
#> 5                                                                         The same bands, later in the ride
#> 6                                                                                             A shared tail
#> 11 Ride it the same way every time. Chained comparisons assume the bridge meter reads the same on both days
